title: Revving Success With Meta’s APSC
subtitle: Leveraging the Power of Advantage+ Drives ROAS and Sales Growth for an Ecommerce Brand
table: Meta’s new initiative brings with it unknown outcomes
Supplemented with APSC to maintain detailed targeting
New technology only allows country-wide geographic targeting
Set spending caps to protect retargeting campaigns
This new technology is relatively untested, posing a risk to campaigns
High level of control in account setup and budget allocation ensured a targeted strategy
insights: As powerful as AI may be, it can’t replace the human touch. AI excels in certain areas, but it’s not a one-size-fits-all solution for every brand. One key factor that contributed to APSC’s success was our decision to use it as a supplemental campaign to the existing account setup. APSC wouldn’t have accomplished the same impressive results without the initial support of our experts who laid the foundation and structured campaigns to meet expectations.
story_head: How a parts maker grew ROAS with Advantage+
story: Meta made Advantage+ shopping campaigns (APSC) widely available in mid-2023. This is part of Meta’s Advantage+ product lineup which utilizes automation to help advertisers more efficiently sell their products online.

To test this new feature, Adtaxi selected a group of national ecommerce brands including this client, a premium manufacturer of motorcycle parts. The introduction of this new technology was a bold risk and meant potential challenges had to be considered before implementation like unknown outcomes, limitations targeting specific regions and locations, and a risk to their campaigns utilizing this new and relatively untested technology.

Adtaxi’s goal was clear: to significantly improve its digital marketing performance. We needed a strategy that would not only increase web traffic but also enhance customer engagement, boost conversion rates, drive sales growth, and generate a higher ROAS. Adtaxi implemented APSC as a supplement to other campaigns and set an aggressive spending cap on the budget. Our team didn’t concentrate all our efforts on APSC and instead decided to maintain a high level of control over the setup and budget allocation.
A manufacturer of premium quality and superior motorcycle parts was looking to optimize its marketing efforts, drive online sales, and increase ROAS in a competitive marketplace.

The client partnered with Adtaxi to expand its marketing efforts and drive campaign performance. As part of Adtaxi’s strategy, we decided to leverage Meta’s APSC, a new system for national ecommerce brands that have product catalogs set up within the Meta platform.

APSC uses automation to help brands maximize campaigns and sell their products online as efficiently as possible. Adtaxi tapped into APSC, testing this new system on a select group of ecommerce clients. This manufacturer was part of our test group, as it met APSC’s requirements, being an ecommerce brand with product catalogs already set up within Meta’s platform.

Utilizing this new technology for the client’s campaign was a risk, as APSCs provided us with far less control in targeting demographics. The limited targeting control only allowed for country-wide geographic targeting. Another pain point utilizing APSC was the possibility of competing with other audiences in the established funnel. This highlighted the importance of understanding and targeting our specific customer base effectively. APSC, while promising innovative changes and updates, means relatively new and untested technology. This posed a risk not only to the success of our client’s campaigns but also to our agency’s relationship with them.

Implementing APSC was a tricky process, especially when trying to balance client goals with potential pain points. To overcome this challenge, Adtaxi came up with a clever solution - implementing APSC as a supplement to other campaigns in the account. Adtaxi implemented aggressive spending caps on the budget spent on existing customers.

This approach ensured that we did not cannibalize our retargeting campaigns and waste valuable resources. Testing this new system, we came to realize the importance of taking a calculated risk. Going all in with APSC wasn’t the best option. Instead, we decided to maintain a high degree of control in account setup and budget allocation. In addition, with real-time monitoring, Adtaxi was able to quickly make changes and adjustments to ensure the success of the client’s campaigns.

The campaign results were exceptional, exceeding expectations within the short four-month period. There was an increase in ROAS from 7.92x to 11.82x over two months. Also, purchase revenue increased from $71,253.98 to $181,745.59, and purchase volume increased from 134 to 355.
